To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the reflection scattering length can be calculated analytically from a universal effective potential for shallow two-body quantum states, and that ab initio calculations show that alpha particles compress when reflected from a hard surface.

the reflection scattering length of two-body states is a universal quantity for a large class of two-body systems and that the compression of a composite body can be calculated ab initio using a new method.

(1) the reflection scattering length can be expressed in terms of the binding energy of the bound state, the binding energy of its first excited state and the effective range, (2) the reflection scattering lengths for two-body states with different binding energies can differ by up to a factor of four, (3) the reflection scattering is universal in the sense that it is independent of the details of the interaction, and (4) the reflection scattering can be used to probe the structure of composite particles.
